summary: Dispatcher for every `kb` subcommand: parseKbArgs collects flags into a KbFlags struct, then a verb switch routes to a cmd* function (search/lookup/write/status/lint/render/view/commit/init/migrate). VERIFIED 2026-07-25 while adding `kb flow-decision`: adding a subcommand takes three coordinated edits that are easy to do incompletely - a field on the KbFlags interface, a case in the parseKbArgs flag switch, and a case in the verb switch - and missing any one fails silently rather than erroring, because unknown flags are skipped and an unmatched verb falls through. Metrics are appended through logMetric from ./store.js, which is already imported here and is best-effort by contract (it must never break a query), so a metrics-only subcommand needs no new dependency.

summary: The kb CLI command table. Two things changed here 2026-07-31. The flow-decision metric no longer needs its own invocation: recordFlowDecision() is shared, and `kb write` fires it whenever --decision is passed, so a capture costs one call instead of two. The standalone `kb flow-decision` subcommand deliberately survives for the one case a flag on write cannot cover — the agent decided NO note was warranted, so there is no write to ride on. Note that --id is overloaded on the merged path (it means the flow id for the decision record), which is safe only because the write path takes the note id from the spec JSON, not from a flag. Also: cmdWrite now emits flowStepsWarning alongside flowEvidenceWarning; warnings accumulate into one array and print as `warning:` lines under the `kb write: <op> → <id>` line, and none of them ever fail the write.

summary: The kb CLI command table. cmdWrite now prints a CAPTURE COVERAGE line under the `kb write: <op> → <id>` line whenever --session is passed and that session has a worklist manifest: 'N of M worklist files noted', the paths still unwritten with their tiers, and — only below 50% — a request to say why they were skipped. It comes from noteCoverage() in session-worklist.ts and is silent when there is no manifest, so a hand-run `kb write` outside capture prints nothing. Chained writes each print it, so the LAST line of the agent's Bash block carries the real tally. Also here: recordFlowDecision() is shared, so `kb write --decision` records the flow metric and a capture costs one call instead of two, while the standalone `kb flow-decision` survives for the wrote-nothing case; --id is overloaded on the merged path (it means the flow id) which is safe only because the write path takes the note id from the spec JSON, not from a flag. Warnings (flowStepsWarning, flowEvidenceWarning) accumulate into one array, print as `warning:` lines, and never fail the write.

summary: The kb CLI command table. cmdWrite is where every post-write signal is assembled: warnings (stepless flow, flow evidence, missing findability fields) accumulate into one array printed as `warning:` lines under `kb write: <op> -> <id>`, then the capture-coverage line. NONE of them ever fails the write — deliberate, because the capture prompt chains writes with && so a non-zero exit silences every note behind the failing one. As of 2026-08-01 cmdWrite re-loads the note after the write (loadNote) and passes its anchor count to flowStepsWarning, so that warning judges the folded result rather than the spec. Coverage comes from noteCoverage() in session-worklist.ts and is silent without --session or a manifest. recordFlowDecision() is shared, so `kb write --decision` records the flow metric and capture costs one call instead of two; standalone `kb flow-decision` survives for the wrote-nothing case, and --id is overloaded there (it means the flow id) which is safe only because the write path takes the note id from the spec JSON. Exit codes are the contract: 0 ok, 1 bad input, 2 not found, 3 candidates.

summary: The kb verb dispatcher — stdout carries only the answer, diagnostics go to stderr; exit 3 means the two-phase write returned candidates. 2026-08-01: new 'repair' verb. It is the only kb verb that deliberately does NOT call ensureKeeper — repair reads the folded notebook and nothing else, so it works in a repo whose keeper never started; an earlier draft awaited the keeper because it needed the symbol sidecar, and dropping that dependency is what makes the command usable on a cold clone. --json prints the {v, notes, findings} report, otherwise repairWorklist's page, and either way exit 0 so a clean notebook is not an error. cmdWrite's warning order is load-bearing: flowStepsWarning is passed the FOLDED note (loadNote after the write), then missingFieldsWarning, then the coverage line last.
